clue.text: Such limited accommodation bringing big store to mind

indicators.note: bringing these words to mind is read as calling up a fresh arrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: A cramped room makes you think wistfully of a big department store.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of BIG STORE TO MIND, rearranged, give the answer; 'bringing ... to mind' is the loose signal that they are to be reworked.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-room flat where you both sleep and sit is the classic example of cramped lodging.

clue.text: Not coming to any conclusion

parts.note: reads like an inconclusive debate, but describes something that never comes to an end

explanation.definitionFit: Something everlasting has no ending at all, so it never reaches a conclusion.

clue.text: Row on out, and find lodgings on either side of the island

indicators.note: on either side says the lodging word sits round the scrambled letters

parts.note: to find lodgings somewhere is to stay there

indicators.note: out says the words row and on are put out of order

explanation.surface: Rowing out to an island and looking for a place to stay at each end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like the rowing in the surface but is anagram fodder. The definition is loose: the answer is the chief town of Lewis in Scotland's Outer Hebrides, standing for the island.
explanation.definitionFit: Stornoway is the main town and port of Lewis, used here as shorthand for that Hebridean island.

clue.text: A muscular joiner

parts.note: suggests a brawny carpenter, but means the tissue that joins a muscle to a bone

explanation.definitionFit: This cord of tough tissue attaches muscle to bone, so it does the joining.

clue.text: I turn mains on — some can't go off because of it

definitions.text: some can't go off because of it

indicators.note: turn tells us to turn the letters of the words around into a new order

explanation.surface: Switching on the mains keeps some people awake.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal 'turn' stands between its fodder words I and MAINS ON; 'go off' means fall asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleeplessness is the condition that stops sufferers dropping off at night.

clue.text: She sounds the type to play a supporting role

indicators.note: sounds says the word for a supporting beam is said out loud to give the name

parts.words: the type to play a supporting role
parts.note: a girder is a beam whose job is to hold things up, cryptically an actor in a supporting role

explanation.surface: A woman seems the sort to take a minor part on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting role' suggests the theatre, but a girder plays its supporting role in a building. In a non-rhotic British accent GIRDER and the girl's name are said alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Gerda is a woman's name, so a female pronoun stands for it.

clue.text: It's hard to take, having our nose put out of joint

indicators.note: a dislocated joint is displaced, so these letters are displaced into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone finds it tough going after a broken nose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' is link material: what is hard to take is described by the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A burdensome task is difficult to bear, which is what hard to take means.

clue.text: Distorted the truth and made President seem right

indicators.note: made is read as made into something else, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone lied by making the head of state look correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' rearranges PRESIDENT, SEEM and R together.
explanation.definitionFit: To give a false account of facts is to twist the truth.

clue.text: Rock bands which ignore hot food when absorbed by clues

indicators.note: absorbed by says the built letters go inside the word clues
Rock is read as a verb: shake the letters of bands into a new order
ignore says one letter is left out of the word which

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Rock groups which avoid hot food when puzzling over crossword clues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' looks like music but is the anagram signal, and 'hot' is the tap abbreviation; 'food' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Multi-layered sandwiches are a kind of food.

clue.text: Admit to having been untruthful and be ordered to go to bed, perhaps

definitions.text: be ordered to go to bed, perhaps

parts.note: having been untruthful means having lied
to own up is to admit

explanation.surface: A child confesses to a fib and is sent to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The charade is in answer order although 'Admit' comes first. A dog ordered to 'lie down' is the picture behind the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To recline, as when told to settle down or turn in, is a command often given to pets or children.

clue.text: Author seen on French river

parts.note: sur is the French word for on
the Tees is a river in north-east England

explanation.surface: A writer spotted on a river in France.
explanation.walkthrough: R. S. Surtees was a Victorian comic novelist of hunting life. 'French' sends the solver to a river in France, but it qualifies 'on'.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Smith Surtees was an English writer, so he is an example of a novelist.

clue.text: Boy in school bedroom link-up with Spanish resort

parts.note: a dorm is a shared bedroom at a boarding school

explanation.surface: A lad in a boarding-school dormitory has a connection with a Spanish holiday town.
explanation.walkthrough: A pun: the three pieces joined up make a phrase one letter away from Benidorm, the Costa Blanca resort.
explanation.definitionFit: The joined phrase nearly spells the name of the Spanish beach town, so it links up with it.

clue.text: Left in a unit but with no company

indicators.note: in says the letter for left is placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: one is a unit, the number one

explanation.surface: Abandoned in a flat with nobody around.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes inside A ONE, between A and ONE. 'Left' looks like the past tense of leave, but is just L.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on your own means having nobody with you.

clue.text: Port I pour into stew

indicators.note: into is read as turned into, so these words are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A cook pours port into a casserole.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of PORT I POUR is signalled by 'into'. 'Stew' is the dish's original sense: the word comes from a Spanish meat stew.
explanation.definitionFit: The term first meant a mixed meat stew, before being used for a medley or scented dried petals.

clue.text: Whip ether out, then medical equipment

parts.note: cat, short for cat-o'-nine-tails, is a whip

indicators.note: out says the letters of ether are put out of order

explanation.surface: Lash out with anaesthetic, then reach for the hospital kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' gives HETER, the anagram of the anaesthetic; the whip is the cat-o'-nine-tails.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin tube put into the body to drain fluids is a piece of hospital apparatus.

clue.text: No locomotion ie train shunted off

indicators.note: shunted off says the letters are pushed out of place like railway wagons

explanation.surface: A train is moved into a siding and goes nowhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is the tendency to stay at rest, so a lack of movement.

clue.text: Pressure on second lock

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Strain applied to a door lock for a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lock' suggests a door, but here it is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress is strain or force, so pressure.

clue.text: Form of spell that is broken

indicators.note: broken says the letters are smashed and put back in a new order

explanation.surface: A kind of magic charm that has been broken.
explanation.definitionFit: An ellipse is a geometric shape, an oval, so a form.

clue.text: Injured bear has eaten American who maltreated him

indicators.note: has eaten says one piece swallows the other
Injured says the letters of bear are damaged into a new order

explanation.surface: A hurt bear has devoured the American who mistreated it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Injured' gives ABER, the anagram of BEAR; 'has eaten' signals the container. The definition reaches back to the bear: its abuser.
explanation.definitionFit: One who mistreats another person or animal is an ill-treater.

clue.text: Part of a wide assortment of notions

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some of a broad range of thoughts.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'of notions' as the definition, but 'of' is a link word: 'notions' alone stands for the plural noun answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Notions are thoughts or concepts in the mind.

clue.text: Wear it for cricket?

definitions.meaning: cricket is an example of a game, the question mark flagging the example

explanation.definitionFit: To display clothing is to sport it, and cricket is one example of an athletic game.

clue.text: Find bogy using steel tool —! and almost lose one's sight

parts.note: a hob is a steel cutting tool used to shape gear teeth

indicators.note: almost says the phrase loses its last letter

parts.note: to lose one's sight is to go blind

explanation.surface: Searching for a ghost with a steel implement and nearly going blind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' signals dropping the final letter of a two-word phrase. The stray '—!' is print debris; 'Find' and 'using' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A bogy is a mischievous spirit or bugbear, the same kind of creature as an imp.

clue.text: Is so small an amount morally acceptable, one feels?

definitions.meaning: a tiny apothecaries' weight, twenty grains
a qualm of conscience is what tells one whether something is morally acceptable

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a tiny old unit of weight and a moral qualm about right and wrong.
